abstract: The safety of foodborne nanoparticles has attracted significant attention in recent years. Previous studies have shown that banana-derived starch nanoparticles (BSNs) can disrupt intestinal barrier function and induce low-grade colitis in healthy mice. However, the in vivo role of these BSNs in intestinal inflammation remains unclear. Here, we show that oral exposure to BSNs aggravated the condition of the mice with DSS-induced colitis. Specifically, BSNs shortened colon length, elevated pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, and exacerbated intestinal barrier damage in mice with colitis. Mechanistic studies revealed that BSNs exacerbated the impairment of tight junction structure and the imbalance of gut microbiota homeostasis. However, native banana starch was shown to alleviate intestinal barrier damage and mitigate colitis by increasing the relative abundances of Akkermansia and Oscillospira . Our findings demonstrate that individuals with colitis or bowel dysfunctions should exercise caution when consuming food rich in resistant starch to minimize potential adverse health effects.

title: Computational refinement for structural identification of catechins and oxidation products in Chinese black tea
abstract: Characterization of natural products and their metabolites in foods is hindered by isomeric ambiguity, limited authentic standards, and compounds absent from libraries. Here, this study presents a confidence-stratified identification workflow adapted from Metabolomics Standards Initiative (MSI) Levels 1–4, spanning standard-confirmed identification, putative annotation, tentative structural or class assignment, and pathway-supported characterization of unknowns. Using UHPLC-QTOF, the workflow was applied to catechins and their oxidation products in Chinese black tea. 27 compounds were confirmed at MSI Level 1 using an in-house library, while 16 oxidation products were annotated at Level 2 by integrating public libraries with SIRIUS-based formula prediction, structure ranking, and class annotation. For compounds absent from libraries, a pathway-informed in-silico pipeline constrained structural space and enabled tentative annotation at MSI Levels 3–4. The approach was further exemplified using oxidation products of theasinensin A and theaflavic acid, reducing the number of chemically plausible candidates for these unknown features.

title: Quantitative lipidomics reveals differences in oil metabolism and nutritional profiles of soybeans with various seed coat colors
abstract: Soybean seeds are rich in high-quality lipids. However, the oil content, differential metabolic pathways, and nutritional characteristics of soybeans with different seed coat colors remain unclear. In this study, the oil content of 169 soybean accessions, including yellow, green, brown, and black soybeans, was determined using the Soxhlet extraction. The results revealed a negative association between oil content and seed coat pigmentation, with yellow seeds exhibiting the highest oil content and black seeds the lowest. Metabolomic analysis of two representative accessions from each seed coat color group showed that lipid subclasses were consistently involved in the significantly altered metabolic pathways across soybean color groups. Subsequent quantitative lipidomic profiling of the 8 accessions identified 650 lipid species belonging to 5 major classes and 26 subclasses. HPLC quantification further showed that total lipid content decreased progressively with increasing seed coat pigmentation, mainly due to changes in triglycerides (TGs), phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs), phosphatidylcholines (PCs), and phosphatidylinositols (PIs). In addition, 38 differentially accumulated lipids were identified between common yellow and black soybeans, and these lipids were significantly enriched in the sphingolipid metabolism pathway. Overall, this study elucidates the relationship between soybean seed coat color and oil composition, providing a potential scientific basis for the functional utilization and dietary application of different color soybeans.

title: AI-guided discovery of fungal-derived salty and saltiness-enhancing peptides for sodium-reduced foods
abstract: Natural salty and saltiness-enhancing peptides are promising candidates for sodium reduction in food systems. This study established an integrated AI-guided workflow combining in silico hydrolysis, embedding-based machine learning, electronic tongue validation, cellular evaluation, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation to identify fungal-derived saltiness-modulating peptides. A taste-active peptide dataset was constructed, and Uni-Mol, ESM-3, and MolCLR embeddings were compared using the same FT-Transformer framework. ESM-3 showed the most favorable classification performance and was selected for screening peptides generated from 14 fungal proteomes. Six candidates were synthesized, including the salty peptides AGHQR, AHDQY, and SKPGNR, and the saltiness-enhancing peptides IPVVVDL, DNNEEW, and ANSDL. Electronic tongue analysis identified AHDQY as the strongest salty peptide in deionized water and ANSDL as the most effective saltiness enhancer in a low-salt NaCl system. These peptides exhibited good cytocompatibility and protected HUVECs against high-salt-induced cellular injury to varying degrees, as evidenced by restored nitric oxide (NO) production and reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations further supported their stable interactions with the transmembrane channel-like protein 4 (TMC4) and peptide-induced modulation of local receptor flexibility and secondary structure. These findings provide promising fungal-derived peptide candidates and a systematic strategy for developing natural saltiness-modulating ingredients for sodium-reduced foods.

title: Nova was never built for the populations it claims to protect
abstract: The Nova classification system has achieved remarkable global traction as the primary instrument for identifying ultra-processed foods in research and dietary policy. Yet the populations Nova purports to protect, those most exposed to food-industry expansion, least able to access alternatives and most burdened by diet-related disease, may be those for whom the framework is least suitable. Nova’s Group 4 designation relies on culturally specific and operationally imprecise criteria that elevate the culinary norms of high-income, food-secure populations into a framework presented as universally applicable. The resulting classification cannot be applied consistently, produces regulatory proposals that cannot be consistently enforced, and generates guidance that is often difficult to implement in the populations most affected by diet-related disease. This Perspective argues that Nova, as currently constituted, is best suited to populations with the resources to act on its recommendations and that progress will require either a more rigorous and reproducible successor framework or clearer recognition of the limits of the current one.

title: Valorization of yak bone collagen byproducts: computational screening and experimental validation of anti-aging peptides targeting MMP-1
abstract: Valorization of yak collagen byproducts offers a sustainable route to food-derived bioactive peptides. To prioritize candidate peptides from yak collagen-derived sequences, we developed AgeAttnMLP, an ESM-2-based screening model that achieved an AUC of 0.891 under conventional five-fold cross-validation and 0.879 under an additional cluster-aware grouped evaluation. Screening of yak collagen sequences followed by Alcalase-guided in silico hydrolysis identified TGPPGPSGI, GEPGAPGE, and GPSGEPGTA as lead candidates. GEPGAPGE showed the strongest MMP-1 inhibition, with an IC 50 of 126 μg/mL. Molecular dynamics simulations and MM-PBSA analysis suggested that peptide binding destabilized the β-sheet spanning residues 76–78 near the catalytic region, potentially affecting substrate recognition. Under the tested conditions, all three peptides extended the lifespan of Caenorhabditis elegans, with the greatest effect observed for GPSGEPGTA at 7.5 mg/mL. These findings establish an integrated computational–experimental strategy for discovering collagen-derived peptides and support the value-added utilization of yak collagen byproducts as potential functional food ingredients.

title: Food and packaging applications of black soldier fly larvae fractions: from processing and functionality to safety and consumer acceptance
abstract: Black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) provide multiple processing-defined fractions for food and food-contact applications. This review evaluates four major fractions: (1) proteins for nutritional and techno-functional applications, (2) lipids for formulation, (3) peptide-rich fractions with candidate bioactivities, and (4) chitin/chitosan for food-contact materials. Protein fractions have the broadest direct food application evidence, while translation requires food safety validation and consumer evaluation across sensory response stated willingness and indirect food pathways.

title: Comprehensive characterization of shilajit from varied provenance: elemental profile, urolithin A content, and antimicrobial activity
abstract: Shilajit is an exudate rich in humic substances that collected from rocks in several mountain ranges and has been used for centuries in traditional medicine for fatigue, physical performance, and general vitality. Ten shilajit samples from five mountain regions (Himalayas, Andes, Altai, Caucasus, and Carpathians) were assessed by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), elemental composition by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), urolithin A (Uro-A) content by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and antimicrobial activity by broth microdilution against five bacterial and five fungal species. DSC identified two distinct thermal groups: seven samples showed only melting transitions between 100–159 °C, while three samples exhibited low-temperature crystallization and sub-zero melting. ICP-MS revealed potassium as the dominant macroelement (up to ~95,600 ppm), with essential trace elements (selenium, zinc and iron) and toxic elements [arsenic (0.14–1.34 ppm), cadmium (0.01–0.10 ppm) and lead (0.35–3.01 ppm)] all present at levels well within FDA/WHO tolerable intake thresholds, comparable to background levels reported in common foods such as dark chocolate. Uro-A content was strongly solvent-dependent, ranging from 0.07 to 1.63 ppm in methanol to 3.46–58.46 ppm in a methanol/ethyl acetate mixture. Antimicrobial activity was species-dependent (MIC 3.12–25 mg/mL), limited to Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus and only two fungal strains ( Mucor mucedo and Geotrichum candidum ), with no activity against the Escherichia coli and Proteus mirabilis . These findings support shilajit’s compositional diversity and highlight Uro-A as its most promising bioactive component, warranting further standardization and origin-based sourcing studies for future bioavailability studies for the potential use as a functional food ingredient.

title: Sustainable postharvest vegetable disease management: integrating physiological insights and innovative technologies for quality preservation
abstract: This review summarizes the underlying causes of postharvest diseases in key vegetable crops and describes novel control strategies including biocontrol, natural antimicrobials, physical treatments, and innovative packaging technologies. A sustainable Integrated Postharvest Disease Management (IPDM) approach is proposed, based on overlapping preventive methods designed to reduce postharvest losses and maintain produce quality. The practical value of multi-omic analyses in elucidating mechanisms of pathogenicity and host resistance is also discussed.

title: Association of chrono-nutrition behaviors with cognitive function in middle-aged and older adults
abstract: Chrono-nutrition, as a new branch of nutritional science, examines the health implications of meal timing, frequency, regularity and its coordination with circadian rhythms. Emerging studies highlight the pivotal role of chrono-nutrition behaviors on aging, yet the associations with cognitive function remain inconclusive. Information on chrono-nutrition behaviors was assessed using validated questionnaires. The global and domain-specific cognition were evaluated using a battery of neuropsychological tests. Linear and logistic regression models were employed to assess the associations. False discovery rates (FDRs) were controlled using multiple-comparison corrections. Greater eating frequency and snacks were associated with worse global cognition and poorer memory. With respect to meal timing, nighttime eating ( β = −0.21, 95% CI: −0.33 ~ −0.09, FDR- P = 0.004) and prolonged eating windows ( β = −0.29, 95% CI: −0.38 ~ −0.21, FDR- P < 0.001) were significantly related to worse memory. Regarding the coordination of eating with circadian rhythms, longer morning latency was associated with worse global and attention, whereas longer evening latency was prominently related to better global cognition and memory function ( β = 0.28, 95% CI: 0.19 ~ 0.38, FDR- P < 0.001). Chrono-nutrition behaviors characterized by higher eating frequency, more snacks, nighttime eating, extended eating windows, longer morning latency, and shorter evening latency were associated with poorer cognition, particularly memory function. These findings underscore the importance of chrono-nutrition in cognitive health.

title: Light-vibration synergy during spreading and optimized drying temperature improve machine-harvested beverage-grade green tea quality
abstract: Optimizing the flavor profile of machine-harvested beverage-grade green tea requires a delicate balance between the retention of low-boiling-point volatiles and the progression of thermal reactions. This study demonstrates that a synergistic light-vibration pretreatment combined with drying at 75 °C is a superior strategy to address this challenge. Using quantitative descriptive analysis (QDA), headspace solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HS-SPME-GC-MS), and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), we found that this protocol significantly elevated the total volatile emission to 20301.17 μg/kg. Crucially, it shifted the compositional profile toward esters and terpenes, which serve as the primary contributors to the floral and fruity notes of green tea. A total of 101 volatile compounds were identified, and nine key aroma-active constituents were screened out. These findings not only elucidate the metabolic pathways activated by light-vibration synergy but also provide a scalable and implementable technical solution for the industrial production of high-aroma, machine-harvested beverage-grade green teas.

title: From aroma cue to feeding behavior: Sichuan pepper essential oil aroma stimulates appetite via cognitive and physiological pathways
abstract: Reduced food intake is a key contributor to malnutrition. The sense of smell plays a fundamental role in appetite regulation, and olfactory stimulation with certain spice essential oils can facilitate oral intake. The present study examined three Sichuan pepper (genus Zanthoxylum) essential oil (SPEO) types by assessing their effects on self-reported appetite ( n = 348) and ad libitum food intake ( n = 78) in humans, and on feeding behavior and hypothalamic neuropeptide expression in mice. In humans, exposure to SPEO aromas enhanced general appetite and modulated sensory-specific appetite, and increased total food intake by 15–19% in male participants with a shift toward salty foods. This effect was more pronounced in frequent consumers, supporting a learned, cognitive pathway. Concurrently, in mice, SPEO inhalation significantly promoted acute food intake, which was closely associated with altered mRNA expression profiles of hypothalamic feeding-related neuropeptides (upregulating MCH and orexin, downregulating POMC). Further analysis identified five appetite-enhancing volatile compounds (β-Phellandrene, Linalool, Ocimene, Eucalyptol, Linalyl acetate). Collectively, these findings support the appetite-promoting effect of SPEO aroma and suggest that this effect involves both convergent cognitive and physiological pathways.

title: Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analysis of oligoproanthocyanidins biotransformation by rhizosphere filamentous fungi from tea plant (Camellia sinensis)
abstract: Incomplete degradation of proanthocyanidins (PAs) causes astringency, reduces nutrient bioavailability in foods, and hinders the feed use of agricultural residues, posing a critical challenge to the food industry. Herein, we explored the potential of tea plant rhizospheric fungi from long-term PAs-enriched habitats to degrade oligoproanthocyanidins (OPC). The five isolated fungal strains were capable of utilizing OPC as a carbon source and exhibited growth comparable to that observed in sucrose-based media. Under submerged fermentation, these fungi metabolized OPC, resulting in changes in pH and color that served as indicators. This process yielded eight fungal metabolites with nutritional and antibacterial properties, notably schizostatin, which was produced by the edible mushroom Schizophyllum commune ScCYS1063. Non-targeted metabolomics revealed that OPC degradation was linked to central energy metabolic pathways. Furthermore, transcriptomic analysis indicated the pattern of PAs as a carbon source capable of fueling fumagillin biosynthesis, triggering class-level transcriptional responses of genes encoding monooxygenases, cytochrome P450S, and dioxygenases. Recovered extracellular proteins effectively degraded procyanidin B2, supporting the potential for controlled enzymatic processes to break down OPC. This study highlights the value of harnessing microbial communities from tea rhizosphere to advance biotransformation of natural metabolites, offering novel solutions for the food industry.

title: Caco-2-derived spheroids and organ-on-a-chip for food safety risk assessment: mechanisms of intestinal inflammation induced by 20 nm polystyrene nanoplastics
abstract: Microplastics released from food packaging have become an emerging food safety concern and may contribute to intestinal inflammation. This study employed Caco-2-derived spheroids combined with self-developed microfluidic organ-on-a-chip technology to systematically investigate the effects of 20 nm polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) on oxidative stress and functional homeostasis in the three-dimensional (3D) intestinal epithelial microenvironment. We detected oxidative stress markers, antioxidant capacity, inflammatory factors, and epithelial function indicators; evaluated Villin and ZO-1 expression by immunofluorescence staining; performed metabolomic analysis on chip effluents; conducted styrene-based computational target prediction and exploratory molecular docking, identifying ALOX5 as a computational candidate; and independently analyzed a public IBD single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset using in silico ALOX5 perturbation for exploratory analysis. The results demonstrated that 40 μg/mL and 400 μg/mL PS-NPs could induce oxidative, inflammatory, and epithelial-associated alterations. This study is the first to integrate Caco-2-derived spheroids and organ-on-a-chip for nanoplastic toxicity evaluation, which provides a novel experimental platform and theoretical basis for investigating potential mechanisms underlying nanoplastic toxicity and risk assessment of food-related nanoplastics.

title: Beyond food waste reduction: nutritional contributions of food rescue initiatives. A systematic review
abstract: Food rescue programs offer environmental and social benefits, yet their nutritional impact remains underexplored. This review supports global sustainability efforts by assessing the nutrition-related outcomes of food rescue initiatives. Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search (PubMed., Scopus, Web of Science, and gray literature via Google Scholar), identified English-language peer-reviewed empirical studies evaluating the nutritional outcomes of food rescue programs. Forty-eight studies were included. Five thematic domains emerged: nutritional intake, food security, food basket quality, nutritional status, and nutritional behavior and environment. While improved dietary intake was frequently reported, inadequacies in fiber, vitamins, and minerals persisted. Food security improvements were documented in 11 intervention studies, although baseline food insecurity remained high (46–95.3%). Food basket audits revealed mixed quality, often lacking fresh produce and nutrient-dense foods. Limited anthropometric and biochemical assessments indicated persistent challenges such as obesity and micronutrient deficiencies. Models integrating food provision with education and client-choice models showed more promising outcomes. However, findings suggest the need for standardized, context-sensitive metrics beyond calorie counts to include diet quality and health outcomes. Future initiatives should adopt multi-component approaches, recipient empowerment strategies, and cross-sector collaborations to maximize health benefits and align with global nutrition and sustainability goals.

title: Matrix-derived hypoallergenicity: potential roles of Beta vulgaris polyphenols and betalamic acid in PR-10 allergen modulation
abstract: Cold-pressed apple, carrot, and celery juices retain native PR-10 allergens associated with Pollen-Food Allergy Syndrome, whereas thermal processing can alter allergen recognition while compromising heat-sensitive nutrients and sensory quality. We propose matrix-derived hypoallergenicity, a framework in which food-matrix chemistry may regulate allergen accessibility. Using beetroot ( Beta vulgaris ) as a model matrix, we examine two chemically plausible pathways, polyphenol-derived quinone modification and betalamic-acid-mediated carbonyl chemistry. Neither pathway has been validated in authentic juice systems. This perspective, therefore, defines a testable framework for modulating allergen behavior while preserving nutritional and sensory quality.

title: Profiling of pollen in honey using multispectral imaging flow cytometry
abstract: Pollen identification from honey (melissopalynology) is of great economic and consumer relevance. Traditional microscopy is time-consuming and dependent on expert knowledge, thus limiting high-throughput analyses. We tested whether pollen images generated with Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry (MIFC) classified by machine learning (ML) (convolution neural networks (CNNs) and random forest (RF)) can serve as a fast and reproducible method for identifying pollen in honey. We examined how the classification of honey pollen is affected by images from different matrices (anther and honey samples), how results compare with traditional microscopic analysis and used a set of human-interpretable image features to better explain ML results. The study focused on the six common target pollen in honey Brassica , Castanea , Centaurea , Helianthus , Phacelia and Tilia type. A classifier trained with a combination of anther and honey brightfield and fluorescence images provided the best predictions for 13 monofloral and 10 polyfloral honeys. Yielding pollen identification results comparable to microscopy, three times more pollen can be evaluated, and a measurement time of a maximum of 10 min, the method demonstrates its high potential as a powerful screening tool in melissopalynology.

title: High-voltage cold plasma alleviates chilling injury in green pepper by synergistically regulating antioxidant and membrane lipid metabolism
abstract: Green pepper ( Capsicum annuum L.) is prone to chilling injury (CI) during cold storage at 4 °C, causing quality deterioration. This study investigated the alleviating effect and physiological basis of high-voltage cold plasma (HVCP) on postharvest CI in green pepper. Fruits were treated with HVCP at 50 kV for 30–150 s and stored at 4 °C for 12 days. The 50 kV/60 s condition was most favorable, reducing the CI index by 94.74% and weight loss by 73.54%, while delaying deterioration of texture, color, and chlorophyll content. HVCP induced an early, transient, and reversible moderate accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS); H₂O₂ and O₂⁻ contents increased by 15.59% and 89.82%, respectively, compared with the control on day 2. It also activated the antioxidant enzyme system and ascorbate-glutathione (AsA-GSH) cycle at the transcriptional level, inhibited key enzymes involved in membrane lipid degradation, reduced phospholipid degradation and polyunsaturated fatty acid oxidation, and increased fatty acid unsaturation (U/S ratio) by 22.17% at the end of storage. Correlation and principal component analyses confirmed that HVCP enhanced chilling tolerance by coordinately regulating antioxidant defense and membrane lipid homeostasis, supporting its potential as a green non-thermal preservation technology.

title: Trifluoromethylpyrimidine‑thiosemicarbazide derivatives as novel multifunctional food preservatives for enhancing storage stability of roxburgh rose juice
abstract: In this work, two predominant gas-generating spoilage fungi (labeled as CQ2 and CQ5) were isolated from deteriorated roxburgh rose ( Rosa roxburghii Tratt) juice and identified as Pichia nanzhaoensis and Arxiozyma slooffiae , respectively. Meanwhile, a series of novel trifluoromethylpyrimidine derivatives bearing a thiosemicarbazide group were synthesized. Biological activity evaluation demonstrated that compound 5a showed stronger antimicrobial efficacy against the isolated strains, with the EC 50 values of 10.63 μg/mL (CQ2) and 8.24 μg/mL (CQ5), respectively, than potassium sorbate (both exceeded 100 μg/mL); compound 5a also exhibited superior antioxidant activity, with the IC 50 values of 4.14 μg/mL (DPPH assay) and 2.95 μg/mL (ABTS assay), respectively, surpassing vitamin C (6.38 μg/mL) and trolox (8.04 μg/mL). Molecular docking and 100 ns dynamics simulations validated its stable binding to NADPH oxidase with the ΔE MMPBSA value of −36.458 kJ/mol, and ADMET analysis confirmed its desirable biosafety. In addition, application experiments confirmed that compound 5a effectively suppressed browning, conserved nutrients, and optimized the juice flavor of roxburgh rose juice during storage. Thus, these results suggest that compound 5a is a promising multifunctional preservative with integrated antimicrobial, antioxidant, and antibrowning activities for roxburgh rose juice and other fruit beverages.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses reveal monoterpenoid biosynthesis in Aspergillus cristatus during tea infusion fermentation
abstract: Monoterpenoids are key contributors to the characteristic aromas of fermented tea, but their formation by Aspergillus cristatus remains unclear. In this study, liquid-state fermentation of a tea infusion was tracked through inoculation with A. cristatus , monoterpenoid profiles, sensory analysis, and transcriptomics were generated at three fermentation stages with or without glucose supplementation. A. cristatus promoted monoterpenoid accumulation as fermentation progressed, and glucose supplementation induced earlier and stronger accumulation of key odor-active compounds. Gas chromatography–olfactometry coupled with aroma extract dilution analysis and odor activity value analyses identified linalool, α -terpineol, geranial, neral, geraniol, citronellol, β -ocimene, nerol, and β -myrcene as major odor-active monoterpenoids in TG12. Transcriptomic analysis indicated activation of the MVA pathway, and AcGal4 was identified as a putative regulatory factor associated with Acerg20 and AcTPS . AcTPS was functionally validated in vitro as a nerol synthase. These findings could assist in the targeted regulation of sensory characteristics of fermented tea.

title: Seasonal dynamics in lettuce phyllosphere microbiota and potential transfer to the human gut
abstract: The surface of fresh vegetable leaves harbors diverse microorganisms with the potential to influence human health through the microbiome-food-gut axis. We investigated the ecology of the bacterial and fungal microbiota on green and red lettuces (n = 143) for a 12-month period using high-throughput amplicon sequencing, and assessed the potential transfer of these microbiota to the human gut. Lettuce-associated fungal and bacterial microbiota exhibited substantial temporal variation, converging into two distinct seasonal cycles: early-season (S1) and late-season (S2). Seasonal progression from S1 to S2 increased species richness in season-specific fungal and bacterial taxa, while inducing abundance shifts in persistent fungal taxa and compositional shifts in persistent bacterial taxa. These seasonal dynamics resulted in more complex and stable microbial networks, in which potential pathogen-associated fungal genera were less frequently enriched. Comparative analyses with gut microbiota datasets from 2831 (fungal) and 3254 (bacterial) individuals revealed that lettuce-associated fungal and bacterial taxa were widely detected in the human gut, with bacterial taxa detected more frequently than fungal taxa. Season-specific taxa were detected more frequently than persistent taxa, and microbial assembly in the gut was shaped by both neutral and deterministic processes. Notably, lettuce-associated bacterial taxa predominantly co-occurred with non-plant glycan-degrading commensal bacteria in a season-dependent manner, and enrichment of these co-occurring taxa correlated positively with gut microbiota richness and composition. Our findings provide insights into the ecological linkages between fresh vegetable microbiota and the human gut microbiota through the food-gut axis.

title: Multi-omics analyses unveil the molecular mechanism involving significant bioactive substances of sea buckthorn at various growth years
abstract: Sea buckthorn fruit quality varies with tree age, but the molecular relationships between branches and fruits remain unclear. This study characterized age-dependent changes in fruit quality and branch–fruit associations in 4-year-old, 5-year-old, and 6-year-old sea buckthorn ( Hippophae rhamnoides L.) using phenotypic analysis, targeted and untargeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Fruit weight increased from 0.38 g at 4 years to 0.54 g at 6 years ( p < 0.001), and 6-year-old fruits had the highest redness value (a* = 18.54). Vitamin C decreased from 0.46 to 0.41 g/100 g ( p < 0.001), whereas procyanidin B4 increased from 78.19 to 103.30 ng/100 mg ( p = 0.044). Untargeted metabolomics identified 554 and 238 DEMs in fruit and 1283 and 996 DEMs in branches for the 5-vs.-4-year and 6-vs.-5-year comparisons, respectively. Branch transcriptomics identified 2658 and 2464 DEGs. Integrated WGCNA and pathway analyses revealed distinct age-associated patterns involving PRKAA and PP2C during 4-5 years and MYBP and PIP5K during 5-6 years, which were associated with fruit metabolite changes. These findings indicate age-dependent coordination between branch molecular responses and fruit quality and provide a basis for optimizing sea buckthorn harvesting and utilization.
